articles.title: AI safety: Silicon Valley's fear narrative meets its governance gap
articles.titleCn: AI安全：硅谷的恐惧叙事与治理鸿沟
articles.summary: AI safety: Silicon Valley's fear narrative meets its governance gap
articles.summaryCn: 文章揭示硅谷AI公司在发出生存威胁警告的同时加速商业化的矛盾，并对比中国在AI治理方面的务实举措，指出真正的治理挑战在于行业能否可信地自我监管。

But the more {{2}} story is not why one researcher left – it is why the industry's most safety-conscious talent can only express concern by quitting. Coxon's warning arrived during the same week that Anthropic was finalizing preparations for what could become the largest IPO in market history. Anthropic filed a {{3}} S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on June 1, targeting a {{4}} of $965 billion, and expects to complete its listing before the US midterm elections in November. Nvidia is in talks to {{5}} the offering at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters reports.

消失的安全承诺
Anthropic首席执行官达里奥·阿莫代伊曾公开呼吁放缓AI发展，以便安全系统能够跟上，然而其公司的IPO时间表却未见相应的减速。2026年2月，Anthropic发布了其《负责任扩展政策》3.0版本，放弃了此前关于若风险无法充分缓解则暂停模型训练的承诺。“暂停训练”的承诺从文件中悄然消失，取而代之的是关于“负责任发展”和透明度机制的更温和措辞。正如中国科技新闻媒体36氪的一篇分析所指出的，Anthropic的安全红线已变得可以动态调整。这正是AI安全辩论核心的结构性矛盾。

Companies warn of civilizational risk while racing to {{12}} the technology at {{13}} speed. Against this backdrop of corporate contradictions and regulatory delays, China's approach has been notably different in method, if not always in pace. articles.fullText:
When Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic in September and warned that artificial intelligence (AI) could end human civilization, his post drew over 170 million views in 48 hours. But the more revealing story is not why one researcher left – it is why the industry's most safety-conscious talent can only express concern by quitting.
Coxon's warning arrived during the same week that Anthropic was finalizing preparations for what could become the largest IPO in market history. Anthropic filed a confidential S-1 with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on June 1, targeting a valuation of $965 billion, and expects to complete its listing before the US midterm elections in November. Nvidia is in talks to anchor the offering at a $2 trillion valuation, Reuters reports.
The safety pledge that disappeared
Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has publicly called for slowing AI development so safety systems can catch up, yet his company's IPO timetable shows no corresponding deceleration. In February 2026, Anthropic released Version 3.0 of its Responsible Scaling Policy, which dropped the company's earlier commitment to pause model training if risks could not be adequately mitigated.
The "pause training" pledge simply disappeared from the document, replaced by softer language about "responsible development" and transparency mechanisms. As an analysis from Chinese technology news outlet 36Kr noted, Anthropic's safety red lines have become dynamically adjustable.
This is the structural contradiction at the heart of the AI safety debate. Companies warn of civilizational risk while racing to commercialize the technology at unprecedented speed.
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman captured the irony bluntly, comparing Anthropic's approach to fear-based marketing: "It is clearly incredible marketing to say, 'We have built a bomb. We are about to drop it on your head. We will sell you a bomb shelter for $100 million to run across all your stuff, but only if we pick you as a customer.'"
Beyond the IPO
The tension between safety rhetoric and commercial behavior extends beyond IPO filings. On September 10 – the same week Coxon's resignation went viral – Anthropic published a 154-page threat intelligence report revealing that its own Claude model had been used for weapons development, military intelligence gathering, cyberattacks and fraud.
Anthropic acknowledged that its safety mechanisms, while blocking some violations, could not fully prevent misuse. The company also restricted access to its most powerful model through Project Glasswing, limiting it to roughly 200 organizations. And after a US Commerce Department order, it excluded foreign nationals entirely, including the EU's cybersecurity agency ENISA.
The governance gap is not confined to corporate boardrooms. The UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI warned in July that AI is "outpacing both scientific understanding and governments' ability to adapt." The panel specifically flagged a phase of "agentic" autonomy that current oversight frameworks cannot manage, potentially allowing dangerous capabilities to emerge before governments can respond.
The EU has delayed compliance deadlines for high-risk AI systems from August 2026 to December 2027, citing the need for more preparation time for standards and regulatory infrastructure.
A different governance model
Against this backdrop of corporate contradictions and regulatory delays, China's approach has been notably different in method, if not always in pace. China's management measures on generative AI services, implemented in August 2023, were the world's first official regulations governing generative AI services. As of July, 1,028 large model services had completed registration, with applications covering industry, agriculture, commerce, education, transportation and law.
The country's AI Safety Governance Framework, now entering its 3.0 version, translates principles of "classification, agile governance and shared governance" into actionable implementation plans, addressing risks from both the technology itself and its applications.
China's "Qinglang" internet government initiative has cleaned up over 5.61 million pieces of illegal information, dealt with more than 49,000 accounts and shut down over 2,400 violating websites and applications related to AI misuse. The country also established the World AI Cooperation Organization in July, with 29 founding member states, and pledged 5,000 AI training opportunities for developing countries over the next five years.
A CGTN global survey found that 85.4% of respondents believe AI's rapid development is creating new challenges for global security and governance. Some 92.6% expressed concern that deepfakes and AI-generated misinformation could erode social trust, and 82.6% believe developing countries and the Global South should play a greater role in shaping AI governance rules.
The real question is not whether AI safety concerns are genuine – they are. The question is whether an industry that produces existential warnings while racing toward trillion-dollar valuations can credibly govern itself. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun put it directly on Monday: "AI development concerns the common well-being of all humanity. All parties should work together to promote open, inclusive and beneficial AI. Spreading various threat narratives and engaging in confrontation and malicious competition will only disrupt the global AI governance process and serve no one's interests."

articles.title: China unites Global South for new chapter of BRICS cooperation
articles.titleCn: 中国团结全球南方，开启金砖合作新篇章
articles.summary: With greater BRICS cooperation entering a new stage of high-quality development, Xi outlined how the grouping can play a more active role in a world marked by growing uncertainty and transformation.
articles.summaryCn: 中国国家主席习近平出席在印度新德里举行的第十八届金砖国家峰会，呼吁金砖国家在推动更加公正合理的国际秩序中发挥先锋作用，开启全球南方合作新篇章，并提出深化合作的五项倡议。

paragraphs.en:
Welcome slogan outside the main venue of the 18th BRICS Summit held from September 12 to 13, 2026, New Delhi, India. /CMG
At the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chinese President Xi Jinping attended the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India from September 12 to 13, calling on BRICS countries to take the {{0}} role in promoting a more just and {{1}} international order and {{2}} in a new chapter of cooperation among the Global South. This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation. What began as an economic concept in a research report has grown into an important force shaping the international {{3}}. With greater BRICS cooperation entering a new stage of high-quality development, Xi outlined at the summit how the grouping can play a more active role in a world marked by growing {{4}} and transformation.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年9月12日至13日在印度新德里举行的第十八届金砖国家峰会主会场外的欢迎标语。/CMG 应印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪邀请，中国国家主席习近平于2026年9月12日至13日出席在印度新德里举行的第十八届金砖国家峰会，呼吁金砖国家在推动更加公正合理的国际秩序方面发挥先锋作用，开启全球南方合作新篇章。今年是金砖合作二十周年。金砖合作最初只是研究报告中的一个经济概念，如今已发展成为塑造国际格局的重要力量。随着大金砖合作进入高质量发展新阶段，习近平在峰会上阐述了金砖国家如何在充满不确定性和变革的世界中发挥更积极的作用。

paragraphs.en:
Be a pioneer in the changing world
The world is undergoing {{5}} changes unseen in a century. Even as the Global South gains strength and multipolarity becomes an {{6}} trend, {{7}} and power politics are resurfacing, posing growing challenges to {{8}} and the international order. Addressing the summit in New Delhi, Xi called on BRICS countries to "stand firmly on the right side of history, strive to be a pioneer of our times, steer the international order in a direction that is more just and equitable, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity."
"To bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical {{9}}, rally the Global South, be an active, {{10}} and positive force in international affairs and advance the well-being of all humanity," Xi said. As to the future development of BRICS, Xi urged the grouping to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development, upholding peace and stability, {{11}} mutual learning between civilizations and reforming and improving global governance. The four pioneering roles align closely with the Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative proposed by China, offering a clear roadmap for BRICS cooperation and a better world.

At the invitation of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Chinese President Xi Jinping attended the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, India from September 12 to 13, calling on BRICS countries to take the pioneering role in promoting a more just and equitable international order and usher in a new chapter of cooperation among the Global South.
This year marks the 20th anniversary of BRICS cooperation. What began as an economic concept in a research report has grown into an important force shaping the international landscape.
With greater BRICS cooperation entering a new stage of high-quality development, Xi outlined at the summit how the grouping can play a more active role in a world marked by growing uncertainty and transformation.
Be a pioneer in the changing world
The world is undergoing profound changes unseen in a century.
Even as the Global South gains strength and multipolarity becomes an irreversible trend, unilateralism and power politics are resurfacing, posing growing challenges to multilateralism and the international order.
Addressing the summit in New Delhi, Xi called on BRICS countries to "stand firmly on the right side of history, strive to be a pioneer of our times, steer the international order in a direction that is more just and equitable, and work together to build a community with a shared future for humanity."
"To bring stability to the world and make it a better place, BRICS countries must seize the historical initiative, rally the Global South, be an active, stabilizing and positive force in international affairs and advance the well-being of all humanity," Xi said.
As to the future development of BRICS, Xi urged the grouping to pioneer in advancing innovation-driven development, upholding peace and stability, facilitating mutual learning between civilizations and reforming and improving global governance.
The four pioneering roles align closely with the Global Development Initiative, Global Security Initiative, Global Civilization Initiative and Global Governance Initiative proposed by China, offering a clear roadmap for BRICS cooperation and a better world.
Xi's remarks reflect the four global initiatives are being translated into more concrete action through BRICS cooperation, providing a broader platform for the Global South to participate in global governance, said Joseph Kimuli, a Ugandan expert on international affairs.
Deepening practical cooperation
BRICS emerged amid the collective rise of emerging markets and developing countries.

Today, BRICS countries span four continents and account for nearly half of the world's population, about 30% of global economic output and more than half of global economic growth, making the grouping a flagship of unity and cooperation among Global South countries.
In his address at the first session of the summit on September 12, Xi said solidarity and cooperation have always been the source of strength for the cause of BRICS throughout its 20-year journey.
He called on member countries to treat each other with candor and sincerity, seek common ground while shelving differences, respect each other's core concerns, stay committed to communication and dialogue to increase mutual understanding and properly handle disagreements.
Speaking at the second session on September 13, Xi proposed five initiatives to deepen BRICS cooperation, covering open source and inclusive artificial intelligence, trade and investment facilitation, digital industry cooperation, intelligent manufacturing cooperation and science and technology talent development.
While the "four pioneers" set out the broader direction for BRICS to contribute to global development, peace, civilization and governance, the five initiatives focus on turning that vision into concrete cooperation. They target emerging areas with direct implications for economic growth and development, offering a more practical action plan for members to work together.
For Global South countries, such cooperation is already creating new opportunities. Sizo Nkala, a researcher at the University of Johannesburg's Center for Africa-China Studies, noted that China's efforts to advance technological and industrial cooperation under the BRICS framework are opening up tangible development opportunities for countries across the Global South. German artificial intelligence expert Stefan Lubich described the new ideas and proposals put forward by Xi as a driving force for the development of emerging industries worldwide.
Toward a third golden decade
China will assume the BRICS presidency next year and host the 19th BRICS Summit, Xi announced at this year's event.
As China prepares to take up the baton, Xi said China is ready to "work with all parties to plan for the future" and "usher in the third golden decade of BRICS cooperation."
The task ahead is to turn the group's growing influence and expanded membership into more effective cooperation and tangible outcomes for the Global South.
Sergey Sanakoyev, president of the Asia-Pacific Research Center in Russia, said he expects China to work with Global South countries to turn the BRICS spirit of openness, inclusiveness and win-win cooperation into more concrete results.

articles.summaryCn: 2026年中国国际服务贸易交易会在北京首钢园举办，展示了中国服务贸易向知识密集型、高附加值和创新驱动方向转型的最新趋势。

paragraphs.en:
The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) will be held at Beijing's Shougang Park from September 9 to 13, offering a window into the latest trends {{0}} China's service trade. As the first national-level {{1}} exhibition for trade in services held in the opening year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), this year's CIFTIS has {{2}} its exhibition format and service model. A total of 90 countries, regions and international organizations will {{3}} in the event, while more than 1,830 companies will attend the exhibitions offline, including 473 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders. The fair will feature more than 190 forums, conferences and business {{4}} activities, alongside 74 supporting events and 11 business inspection routes. Knowledge-{{5}} services as a new engine
Knowledge-intensive services have been increasingly driving China's service exports.
paragraphs.cn: 2026年中国国际服务贸易交易会（服贸会）将于9月9日至13日在北京首钢园举行，为人们了解重塑中国服务贸易的最新趋势提供了一个窗口。作为“十五五”规划开局之年（2026—2030年）举办的首个国家级综合性服务贸易展会，今年的服贸会升级了展览形式和服务模式。共有90个国家、地区和国际组织将参加此次活动，超过1830家企业将线下参展，其中包括473家《财富》世界500强企业和行业领军企业。本届服贸会将举办190多场论坛、会议和商务对接活动，以及74场配套活动和11条商务考察路线。知识密集型服务成为新引擎，知识密集型服务日益推动中国服务出口。

paragraphs.en:
In the first half of 2026, the country's total service imports and exports reached 3.8 trillion yuan (about $566.2 billion), up 8.3% year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce. Among them, exports of intellectual property {{6}}, financial services, transport services, and telecommunications, computer and information services grew 44.3%, 25.9%, 25.4% and 10.9%, respectively. Knowledge-intensive services {{7}} for 53.5% of total service exports, increasing 3 percentage points from the end of 2025. The figures show that China's service trade is shifting toward higher-value-added and technology-intensive {{8}}, said Zhao Ruojin, an associate researcher at the Institute of International Service Trade under the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation. From exporting products to delivering technologies and services
The Information and Communication Exhibition at this year's China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS).
paragraphs.cn: 据商务部数据，2026年上半年，我国服务进出口总额达到3.8万亿元人民币（约5662亿美元），同比增长8.3%。其中，知识产权使用费、金融服务、运输服务以及电信、计算机和信息服务出口分别增长44.3%、25.9%、25.4%和10.9%。知识密集型服务占服务出口总额的53.5%，较2025年底提高3个百分点。中国国际贸易经济合作研究院国际服务贸易研究所副研究员赵若锦表示，这些数据表明中国服务贸易正朝着更高附加值和科技密集型领域转变。从出口产品到输出技术与服务，今年中国国际服务贸易交易会的信息与通信展区。

paragraphs.en:
Wang Chulun
The transformation is closely linked to the deeper {{9}} of manufacturing and services. Chinese companies are increasingly moving from simply exporting goods to providing integrated technologies, solutions and full-cycle services. One example comes from the aviation maintenance sector in south China's Hainan Province. {{10}} the policy advantages of the Hainan Free Trade Port, the Haikou Airport Comprehensive Bonded Zone has established specialized aircraft and aero-engine maintenance facilities, {{11}} five leading aviation maintenance companies and holding 24 international maintenance licenses covering 19 countries and regions, as well as more than 2,300 component maintenance {{12}}. During this year's summer travel season, overseas aircraft arrived for maintenance.
paragraphs.cn: 王楚伦。这一转变与制造业和服务业更深层次的融合密切相关。中国企业正日益从单纯的商品出口转向提供集成技术、解决方案和全周期服务。一个例子来自中国南方海南省航空维修领域。依托海南自由贸易港的政策优势，海口空港综合保税区建立了专业的飞机和航空发动机维修设施，入驻了五家领先航空维修企业，持有覆盖19个国家和地区的24项国际维修许可证，以及2300多项部件维修认证。在今年暑运期间，境外飞机前来维修。

paragraphs.en: "Airlines from Qatar, Jordan, Thailand and Vietnam have become repeat customers," said Guo Luoyi, a business manager at Grand China Aviation Maintenance Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of HNA Technic, noting that overseas maintenance orders are expected to exceed 100 aircraft this year. "China's service exports are shifting from traditional sectors such as engineering and transportation to the export of high value-added capabilities, including knowledge, creativity and other high value-added services," said Lin Xuejun, a professor at the International Business School of Jinan University. Lin said this transformation is driven by years of innovation {{13}}, with numerous research achievements, patents, and brands developed through new business models and emerging industries providing strong support for intellectual property-related service exports. Innovation will be another highlight of this year's fair. China views digitalization, intelligent technologies, and green development as key drivers of high-quality development and is promoting the application of big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI) across service trade, said Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong at a press conference briefing the media about CIFTIS in August.

The innovation-driven transformation will be showcased in the newly established “China services” exhibition zone, featuring 140 representative cases from domestic regions and enterprises across a broad range of service trade sectors. The demonstrated cases will highlight the expanding global reach of Chinese services, with solutions ranging from BeiDou-based space and time information services and cross-border trade platforms to international pharmaceutical research and development services and logistics solutions. The 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) will be held at Beijing's Shougang Park from September 9 to 13, offering a window into the latest trends reshaping China's service trade.
As the first national-level comprehensive exhibition for trade in services held in the opening year of the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), this year's CIFTIS has upgraded its exhibition format and service model.
A total of 90 countries, regions and international organizations will participate in the event, while more than 1,830 companies will attend the exhibitions offline, including 473 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders. The fair will feature more than 190 forums, conferences and business matchmaking activities, alongside 74 supporting events and 11 business inspection routes.
Knowledge-intensive services as a new engine
Knowledge-intensive services have been increasingly driving China's service exports. In the first half of 2026, the country's total service imports and exports reached 3.8 trillion yuan (about $566.2 billion), up 8.3% year on year, according to the Ministry of Commerce.
Among them, exports of intellectual property royalties, financial services, transport services, and telecommunications, computer and information services grew 44.3%, 25.9%, 25.4% and 10.9%, respectively. Knowledge-intensive services accounted for 53.5% of total service exports, increasing 3 percentage points from the end of 2025.
The figures show that China's service trade is shifting toward higher-value-added and technology-intensive segments, said Zhao Ruojin, an associate researcher at the Institute of International Service Trade under the Chinese Academy of International Trade and Economic Cooperation.
From exporting products to delivering technologies and services
The Information and Communication Exhibition at this year's China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS). Wang Chulun
The transformation is closely linked to the deeper integration of manufacturing and services. Chinese companies are increasingly moving from simply exporting goods to providing integrated technologies, solutions and full-cycle services.
One example comes from the aviation maintenance sector in south China's Hainan Province. Leveraging the policy advantages of the Hainan Free Trade Port, the Haikou Airport Comprehensive Bonded Zone has established specialized aircraft and aero-engine maintenance facilities, accommodating five leading aviation maintenance companies and holding 24 international maintenance licenses covering 19 countries and regions, as well as more than 2,300 component maintenance certifications.
During this year's summer travel season, overseas aircraft arrived for maintenance.
"Airlines from Qatar, Jordan, Thailand and Vietnam have become repeat customers," said Guo Luoyi, a business manager at Grand China Aviation Maintenance Co., Ltd., a subsidiary of HNA Technic, noting that overseas maintenance orders are expected to exceed 100 aircraft this year.
"China's service exports are shifting from traditional sectors such as engineering and transportation to the export of high value-added capabilities, including knowledge, creativity and other high value-added services," said Lin Xuejun, a professor at the International Business School of Jinan University.
Lin said this transformation is driven by years of innovation accumulation, with numerous research achievements, patents, and brands developed through new business models and emerging industries providing strong support for intellectual property-related service exports.
Innovation will be another highlight of this year's fair.
China views digitalization, intelligent technologies, and green development as key drivers of high-quality development and is promoting the application of big data, cloud computing and artificial intelligence (AI) across service trade, said Vice Minister of Commerce Yan Dong at a press conference briefing the media about CIFTIS in August.
More than 200 new products and achievements will be unveiled at this year's CIFTIS, with over 100 making their global or China debut, covering areas including information and communications, fintech, digital healthcare, smart education, and energy conservation and environmental protection.
'China services' expanding through innovation
The innovation-driven transformation will be showcased in the newly established “China services” exhibition zone, featuring 140 representative cases from domestic regions and enterprises across a broad range of service trade sectors.
The demonstrated cases will highlight the expanding global reach of Chinese services, with solutions ranging from BeiDou-based space and time information services and cross-border trade platforms to international pharmaceutical research and development services and logistics solutions.
Nearly 40% of the cases involve AI, large language models, or intelligent agents applied in fields such as legal services, digital trade, cultural tourism and quantum computing.

这些新举措凸显了一种转变，即让贸易和商业成为博览会的核心，让企业成为主要参与者，让实际应用成为关键特色。

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi (R), also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, holds talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Iran Seyyed Abbas Araghchi in Beijing, China, September 16, 2026. 
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held talks with Minister of Foreign Affairs of Iran Seyyed Abbas Araghchi on Wednesday in Beijing, encouraging Iran and the United States to stay rational and exercise restraint, and return to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) at an early date.
Wang, also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, noted China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, is willing to play a constructive role in resolving international disputes.
Noting that China and Iran are comprehensive strategic partners, he said China is ready to work with Iran to strengthen dialogue and cooperation, and safeguard Iran's legitimate rights and interests.
Wang said the continued prolongation of the US-Iran conflict is not in the common interest of the parties concerned and the international community.
China encourages Iran and the US to rebuild the negotiation mechanism on the basis of the consensus reached so far, and conduct substantive consultations on issues of respective concern, Wang said, adding that China supports Iran in engaging in dialogue with Gulf states, respecting each other's territorial sovereignty and national security, and safeguarding the shared regional interests in a constructive manner.
China urges all parties to take effective measures to open the Strait of Hormuz at an early date, safeguard the smooth and safe operation of international shipping routes, and maintain the stability of international energy transport, as well as global industrial and supply chains, he said.
"We do not wish to see regional tensions spill over further into Yemen and the Red Sea," the Chinese foreign minister said, calling on all parties to refrain from further complicating the situation and resolve issues through dialogue and negotiation.
Wang pointed out that current developments have once again proven that the existing security architecture in the Middle East is inadequate, calling for reform and reinforcement.
During his visit to Egypt, Chinese President Xi Jinping raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security, Wang said, adding that China welcomes useful explorations by regional countries in this regard.
On Middle East issues, China, as a responsible major country, will as always contribute to peace and stability, promote peace talks, and uphold fairness and justice, Wang said.
Wang said China's policy toward Iran maintains continuity and consistency, adding that China always upholds justice, opposes the use of force, and safeguards the norms governing international relations within the UN Security Council and other multilateral platforms.
China stands ready to step up communication and coordination with Iran to deliver new progress in China‑Iran relations, he added.
Briefing on the latest situation in the Middle East as well as Iran's considerations for the next steps, Araghchi said Iran does not wish for the conflict to drag on and hopes to return to diplomatic channels, while resolutely safeguarding its own rights and interests.
Iran holds that the US‑Iran MoU remains valid, and has reached an agreement with Oman on a plan to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, he said, adding that the US should earnestly honor all its commitments.
The Iranian side also stands ready to engage in dialogue and consultation with regional countries, establish and develop good-neighborly and friendly relations, and promote the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region, said Araghchi.
He said Iran welcomes and supports President Xi's four‑point proposal, and is ready to work with China to strengthen cooperation, and looks forward to China playing a greater role in promoting regional peace and stability.
Iran attaches great importance to its relations with China and stands ready to continue mutual support, maintain close exchanges at all levels, deepen practical cooperation, jointly address challenges, and push for the sustained and in-depth development of bilateral ties, said the Iranian foreign minister.
